text: The cow's udder consists of four separate quarters, each containing a separate mammary gland made up of: secretory tissue (alveoli); a duct system collecting milk from the alveoli to the cistern; two cisterns (storage areas) — one in the mammary gland holding 250–500 ml of milk, and one in the teat holding 20–40 ml of milk; and a teat containing a cistern, kept closed near the tip by a circular muscle (sphincter).
